Published online:
September 11, 2026

Geographic focus:
India, Middle East (Yemen, Red Sea, Strait of Hormuz), Asia-Pacific (broad)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [NO]
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
Indian equities sold off sharply as Brent crude surged past $108/bbl driven by escalating Middle East conflict — Houthi seizure of Yemen's port of Mocha and intensified tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz. The oil spike is feeding inflation fears globally, pushing bond yields higher (India's 10Y above 7%) and raising the probability of imminent Fed tightening. Fed funds futures are pricing >70% chance of a rate hike next week. Broad-based risk-off is hitting Asia-Pacific equities hard, with Indian small- and mid-caps leading losses. Energy upstream names (ONGC, Oil India) are the lone bright spots.
